relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Judah's remembered line continues through Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Families of Zorah emerge through Reaiah, Jahath, Ahumai, and Lahad.
Hazzelelponi is named beside her brothers, preserving a woman's place in Etam's household.
Hur's descendants connect Gedor, Hushah, Ephrathah, and Bethlehem.
Helah and Naarah are named as wives within Ashhur's household.
Naarah's sons are remembered through her name.
Helah's sons are remembered through her name.
Hakkoz's descendants become families rather than isolated names.
Jabez carries a name born from his mother's pain, yet pain is not his destiny.
He asks for blessing, room to live, Divine presence, and protection from harm; the prayer is heard without becoming a formula.
Chelub, Mehir, and Eshton continue another branch.
Recah's households are remembered through Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah.
Kenaz's line includes Othniel, Seraiah, and Hathath.
The valley of artisans remembers skill as part of communal identity.
Caleb son of Jephunneh's descendants remain distinct from other Caleb traditions.
Jehallelel's four sons remain in the archive.
An unnamed woman bears Miriam and sons while the text leaves her identity unresolved.
Bithiah, daughter of Pharaoh, enters Judah's family memory across national boundaries.
A wife's kin connect Keilah, Garmites, and Maacathites.
Shimon and Ishi's households are named.
Shelah's descendants include families of skilled linen workers.
Ancient records preserve people linked with Moab and Bethlehem.
Potters and gardeners live near royal work, their labor carrying the kingdom's daily life.
Simeon's line begins with five sons.
Shallum, Mibsam, and Mishma continue the branch.
Hammuel, Zaccur, and Shimei continue it further.
One family's different size is recorded without making fertility a measure of worth.
Simeonite settlements begin to map the south.
More towns hold the memory of ordinary habitation.
Bethuel, Hormah, and Ziklag enter the map.
Cities remain connected with Simeon's life until David's reign.
Five villages extend the settlement network.
The genealogy becomes geography: names belong to places and lived communities.
Leaders of expanding families are named.
Joel and Jehu's line is recorded.
A longer list of leaders continues.
Ziza's ancestry is traced through generations.
Family growth produces political leadership.
The search for pasture begins an expansion toward another community's land.
The land is broad, fertile, and peaceful because people already live there.
Pasture-seeking becomes violent dispossession under Hezekiah, and the victims must not disappear beneath victory language.
Five hundred Simeonites move toward Seir under named commanders.
The surviving Amalekite community is struck and its land occupied, a memory that cannot authorize modern killing.

contemplative_note: The chapter places prayer, craft, family growth, pasture, and conquest side by side. Jabez asks to be kept from harm; later groups enlarge their territory by harming peaceful inhabitants. The spiritual test is whether blessing creates room for shared life or becomes a holy name for dispossession.
